explanation: The kinematic point (W=1.7 GeV, Q2=1.0 GeV^2, cos(theta*)=0, phi=90) is physically valid and passes all threshold, cos(theta*) pole-safety, Q2-positivity, beam-energy-accessibility, lookup-table-coverage, phi-range, and vcut-sanity checks. The request specified vcut = -0.1, which is non-standard: negative vcut switches EXCLURAD to its 'v' interpretation (a dimensionless inelasticity variable) instead of the usual positive inelasticity cut in GeV^2. The code does not reject this value; it simply changes the cut semantics. The user explicitly requested this value, so the input was generated as-is. The beam energy defaulted to 6.53 GeV (CLAS12 RG-K, the validated eta campaign); alternative CLAS12 energies of 10.6 GeV (RG-A) and 10.2 GeV (RG-B) are available and yield different radiative corrections. rc_mode is 'full' O(alpha).
